Option A is inaccurate.  
While nsp14 does contain an N-terminal 3′→5′ exonuclease (ExoN) whose activity is strongly stimulated by its co-factor nsp10 and indeed provides a mismatch-repair/​proof-reading function, this enzyme complex does not “prevent the breakdown of dsRNA.”  On the contrary, the ExoN actually excises mis-incorporated nucleotides from the 3′ end of nascent double-stranded RNA, i.e. it performs limited degradation to remove errors rather than preventing RNA degradation.  The other statements (B, C, D) are consistent with current experimental observations on SARS-CoV-2 biology.

Answer: A
